description: Work a story with no test-first step: do the change, verify it against the acceptance criteria, commit, close out.

story.description: the story bead this formula works

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Run whatever {{story}}'s acceptance criteria say to check, and confirm it passes. Run the gate in the foreground: `mw check {{story}}`, or `make test` then `make lint`. Give each mw check call the largest timeout the Bash tool's own description allows, and no `timeout` wrapper: mw check waits inside the call and its last line says when to run it again. If mw check {{story}} names parts of the gate not yet run, run `mw check {{story}} --part N` for each part, one per Bash call and each in the foreground (a part's pass counts only at the commit it ran at, so any later commit, a doc too, makes every part run again: make your last edit first, stop editing by the turn the boot gave you, and run each part once), then `mw check {{story}}` with no part: it runs none of the gate and reports the whole gate green, or the parts that failed or were not run. Never nohup or background it and wait with tail --pid, a sleep loop or polling: the auto-mode classifier refuses that wait and the story stops with its steps open. If a call is cut off with no last line, say so on the bead and hand back. `mw check {{story}}` queues for this host's gate lock, the merge slot and a calm host. When its last line says your place in the queue is kept for 10 minutes, run the same command again in a fresh Bash call, as many times as the session's time allows. Hand back only if a line says the wait limit was reached (do not run the check again then) or when the session's turn cap nears: comment on the bead naming the holder and hand back. A check 'under load' runs under contrib/mw-under-load <command>; never hand-rolled busy loops, stress or yes on a host.

steps.title: Commit
steps.description: Commit the change for {{story}} in small, plainly described commits, with no AI attribution lines.

steps.title: Closing comment
steps.description: Comment on {{story}} with what was done, what was verified and how, and anything left undone. When your diff adds or changes a file under grinds/examples/ (grinds/examples/<kind>/<name>.json), run each such example against the live mill first (`mw grist eval <app> <kind> --example <name>`, with `--ref` your branch) and write a line for it in the comment, 'mw grist eval <app> <kind> --example <name>: PASS': the fake mill is not proof, and a close-out refuses a comment with no such line for an example the branch changed. Before that section, when the story changes something the Governor can see, add a section headed exactly 'HOW TO CHECK IT, for the Governor': at most six plain numbered steps with the exact on-screen labels and what right looks like. Quote every label from the source, never from memory: find it in the component (grep the rig's src/ for it), put it between double quotes, and quote nothing you did not find there. After you comment, run `mw lint-checkit {{story}} --dir .`: it exits non-zero and names each quoted label not found in src/, and then you comment again with the corrected section (the newest HOW TO CHECK IT is the one read); otherwise write the single line 'Internal: nothing for the Governor to look at'. Also give one line, 'What's new: New: <one plain sentence the Governor would understand, no file names>' or 'What's new: Fixed: <one plain sentence, no file names>', or 'What's new: none' for a change he cannot see (tests, docs, internal): mw next writes it into the app's changelog when the rig keeps one. Also add a section headed exactly 'Found, not fixed:', just before the 'For common errors:' section a bug asks for, and before 'For the rig memory:': one line for each problem you saw and did not fix, or the single word nothing. Each line says what is wrong and then file:line, and then, on the same line, these four, in this order: 'AC: <one line checkable by running something, with the command it names>', 'Sweep: <where else the same fault can be, and how to look>', 'Size: <XS, S, M, L or XL, your guess>', and 'By design? yes' or 'By design? no' (say yes when the code's own comment says it is deliberate). For example: 'The parser drops a trailing line (application/parse.go:12). AC: go test ./application -run TestParseKeepsTheLastLine passes. Sweep: the other readers in application/parse*.go. Size: S. By design? no'. You file no beads; mw next files each line as a held bug for the Mayor to word, copying your AC and Sweep into the bug's acceptance and your size into its path; a line with no AC is still filed, held with the reason 'no AC from the Builder', so give one. END the closing comment with a section headed exactly 'For the rig memory:' holding at most two typed facts that a later Builder on this rig would have been saved real time by, one per line, each written as the ready mw memory command that places it (write it, never run it): `mw memory add <rig> --kind gotcha|decision --subject <subject> --source {{story}} "<sentence>"`, `mw memory supersede <rig> <slug> --source {{story}} "<sentence>"`, `mw memory retire <rig> <slug> --reason "<reason>"` or `mw memory recheck <rig> <slug> --why "<why>"` (a slug names a fact the rig memory already holds; add `--slug <name>` to an add or a supersede to name the new fact), or the single word 'nothing'. mw next passes each line to the Mayor as that command with the story as its source, and flags a line it cannot read; the older forms 'gotcha [subject]: <sentence>' and 'retire <slug>: <reason>' are still read. The Builder does NOT edit the rig memory file: the Mayor places what he keeps. Post the comment from a file, never from a heredoc on stdin: write the text to a file and run `bd comments add <id> -f <file>` (bd has no stdin dash, so `bd comments add <id> - <<EOF` posts a literal '-' and the story is refused), then read it back with `bd show <id>` and confirm the whole text is there before you close this step.
